endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Document metadata tagging standards to support filtering, auditing, and corpus management over time.

endorsements.title: Beyond Time Saved: Implementation, Equity, and the Utility Threshold for Nursing AI Scribes
endorsements.quote: Addressing the ASR equity gap rather than treating it as an afterthought requires conducting subgroup analyses by context-specific axes of linguistic variation, including accent, dialect, and professional characteristics as suggested [ 1 ], and disaggregated reporting on adoption, dropout, and equity metrics of ASR performance.

endorsements.title: An Acceptance Criteria Framework for Determining the Implementation Fit of Custom Large Language Models in Public Health Interventions
endorsements.quote: Depending on the project context, prompts might also benefit from specifying health literacy levels, the use of colloquial language, or common informal phrasing to provide more realistic question prompts.

endorsements.title: Using ambient AI in clinical consultations: reframing policy around clinical audit and patient safety
endorsements.quote: Developers should accordingly report WER disaggregated by language and population rather than as a single aggregate figure.

endorsements.title: The Promise of Ambient AI Technology in Medical Education: Opportunities and Guardrails
endorsements.quote: Build equity monitoring into deployment from day 1; teach learners to detect and escalate differential performance; require vendor disclosure of training data and performance disaggregated by patient demographics.

evidence.title: A Multilingual Chatbot Can Effectively Engage Arthroplasty Patients Who Have Limited English Proficiency
evidence.outcome: Chatbot conversational engagement in LEP versus English-primary-language patients
evidence.effect: No difference in engagement between LEP and EPL patients (12.3 vs 12.2 text responses, P = .959).
evidence.quote: There was no difference in the conversational engagement between LEP patients and those with English as their primary language (EPL) (12.3 versus 12.2 text responses, P = .959).

evidence.title: Performance of an Ambient Generative AI Documentation Tool in a Linguistically Diverse Clinical Setting
evidence.outcome: Ambient scribe documentation performance (unedited AI-generated words) by patient language
evidence.effect: Non-English encounters were 21%–25% less likely than English encounters to achieve the same performance threshold; no significant difference between interpreter-mediated and bilingual provider encounters.
evidence.quote: Non-English encounters were 21%–25% less likely than English encounters to achieve the same performance threshold.

evidence.title: Accuracy and error patterns of ChatGPT-4o for real-time English–Nepali voice translation: A cross-sectional field evaluation in rural Nepal
evidence.outcome: Translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4o for English-Nepali voice translation, by direction
evidence.effect: Of 485 translations, 282 (58.1%) highest accuracy, 134 (27.6%) moderate, 69 (14.2%) lowest; 63 of 69 low-accuracy translations (91.3%) occurred in Nepali-to-English direction.
evidence.quote: Of 485 translations, 282 (58.1%) received the highest accuracy rating, 134 (27.6%) a moderate rating, and 69 (14.2%) the lowest.

evidence.title: Using a Multilingual AI Care Agent to Reduce Disparities in Colorectal Cancer Screening for Higher Fecal Immunochemical Test Adoption Among Spanish-Speaking Patients: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: AI outreach engagement (FIT opt-in, connect rate, call duration) stratified by patient language
evidence.effect: Spanish-speaking patients had higher FIT opt-in (18.2% vs 7.1%, P<.001), connect rates (69.6% vs 53.0%), and call duration (6.05 vs 4.03 min) than English-speaking; adjusted OR 2.012 (95% CI 1.340-3.019).
evidence.quote: Spanish-speaking patients demonstrated significantly higher engagement across all measures than English-speaking patients with respect to FIT test opt-in rates (18.2% vs 7.1%, P<.001), connect rates (69.6% vs 53.0%, P<.001), and call duration (6.05 vs 4.03 minutes, P<.001).

evidence.title: A Bilingual Arabic-English Ambient AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Prospective Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Ambient scribe note accuracy compared between Arabic and English encounters
evidence.effect: Accuracy mean 4.53 (SD 0.46) out of 5 for Arabic vs 4.77 (SD 0.37) for English (P=.06); Arabic slightly lower but not significant.
evidence.quote: On the Likert scale, for the accuracy domain, the mean score was 4.53 (SD 0.46) out of 5 for Arabic compared with 4.77 (SD 0.37) out of 5 for English (P=.06).

evidence.title: Ambient AI in primary care: an exploratory mixed methods survey of UK general practitioners
evidence.outcome: Ambient scribe error frequency in non-English encounters
evidence.effect: Errors were most frequent in multiparty consultations (38%), complex histories (35%) and non-English encounters (31%).
evidence.quote: Errors were most frequent in multiparty consultations (38%), complex histories (35%) and non-English encounters (31%).
evidence.sample_unit: GP users of ambient AI scribes (of 1003 survey respondents)

evidence.title: Prompting language influences diagnostic reasoning and accuracy of large language models
evidence.outcome: Diagnostic reasoning and accuracy of LLMs compared between English and French prompts
evidence.effect: Four of five models performed better in English (mean difference 0.37-0.91, adjusted p < 0.05); o3 showed no overall language effect.
evidence.quote: Four of the five models performed better in English (mean difference 0.37-0.91, adjusted p < 0.05), with the gap spanning multiple aspects of reasoning, including differential diagnosis, logical structure, and internal validity.

evidence.title: When Artificial İntelligence Speaks For The Obstetrician: Multilingual Accuracy On Real Patient Questions
evidence.outcome: LLM answer accuracy in Turkish versus English for pregnancy questions
evidence.effect: Gemini and DeepSeek answers to English questions had statistically higher accuracy than Turkish (p < 0.05); ChatGPT showed no general accuracy difference between languages.
evidence.quote: It was found that Google Gemini and DeepSeek's answers to English questions achieved statistically higher accuracy scores than their answers to Turkish questions (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Impact of Query Language on Large Language Model Performance in Dental Trauma Management: A Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude
evidence.outcome: LLM response quality in dental trauma scenarios, English vs Turkish, by model
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 9.14% higher in English (p<0.001, r=0.874); Gemini 5.69% higher in English (p=0.003); Claude no difference (-0.02%, p=0.220).
evidence.quote: Claude exhibited language independence with virtually identical performance in both languages (-0.02%, p = 0.220).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (27 scenarios x 3 models x 2 languages)

evidence.title: Ambient AI Documentation in Mixed-Language Encounters: A Heuristic Evaluation of Reenacted Mandarin–English and Spanish–English Clinical Conversations
evidence.outcome: Transcription mixed error rate by language pair in ambient AI documentation
evidence.effect: Median MER 4% overall with less variation in Spanish–English conversations, and 9% in Mandarin–English conversations, with outliers reaching 67%; deletions frequent at switch points in Mandarin–English transcripts.
evidence.quote: Overall MER was low, with a median of 4% and less variation in Spanish–English conversations, and 9% in Mandarin–English conversations, but with outliers reaching 67%.

evidence.title: Quality, consistency, and clinical safety of AI-generated versus clinician-written clinical notes: a multi-country paired simulation study
evidence.outcome: AI scribe note quality (PDQI-9) versus clinician notes by site/language
evidence.effect: AI notes scored higher than clinician notes in all five sites and languages (dz 0.41–0.75); overall 40.6 vs 35.6, difference +5.08.
evidence.quote: AI notes scored higher than clinician notes on the PDQI-9 (40.6 vs 35.6; difference +5.08, 95% CI 4.6–5.6; Cohen’s dz=0.55), consistently across all five sites (dz 0.41–0.75), and were less dispersed (5.7% of AI vs 27.8% of clinician notes fell below the study pre-specified low-score threshold (<32)).
evidence.country: United Kingdom, Spain, Italy, France, Germany

evidence.title: LUMANA: A Scenario-Based Field Validation of a Culturally Adapted AI System for Mental Health Screening in Sokoto State, Nigeria
evidence.outcome: Hausa transcription, translation, and summary generation quality scores
evidence.effect: Mean 9.9/10 Hausa transcription, 9.9/10 Hausa-to-English translation, 9.2/10 English-to-Hausa summary generation.
evidence.quote: Mean language quality scores were 9.9/10 for Hausa transcription, 9.9/10 for Hausa-to-English translation, and 9.2/10 for English-to-Hausa summary generation.
evidence.sample_unit: stakeholders completing structured evaluations (136 AI output safety assessments across 8 scenarios)

evidence.title: Mind the gap: emergent clinical risk at the interface of two individually safe AI systems in a multilingual ambient scribe
evidence.outcome: End-to-end serious note error incidence by language resource tier
evidence.effect: End-to-end serious errors rose with language scarcity (high 7%, medium 10%, low 15%; OR 1.54 per tier, 95% CI 1.15-2.07; p=0.004), whereas intrinsic note generation showed no detectable language gradient.
evidence.quote: End-to-end serious errors rose steeply with complexity (L1 1% to L4/L5 24%) and language scarcity (high 7%, medium 10%, low 15%; OR 1.54 per tier, 95% CI 1.15-2.07; p=0.004, GEE clustered on language).
evidence.sample_unit: scripted consultation sessions (end-to-end arm; 385 in intrinsic arm)
languages: 77 languages including high-, medium-, and low-resource languages

evidence.title: GPT-4 outperforms ChatGPT in answering non-English questions related to cirrhosis
evidence.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to cirrhosis questions by patient language (English, Korean, Mandarin, Spanish)
evidence.effect: GPT-4 had significantly higher proportions of comprehensive and correct answers than ChatGPT in all four languages (p<0.05). ChatGPT produced erroneous non-English responses. The quality gap between English and non-English answers was smaller with GPT-4.
evidence.quote: GPT-4 showed a marked improvement in the proportion of comprehensive and correct answers compared to ChatGPT across all four languages (p<0.05).
evidence.sample_unit: questions (each translated into 3 languages, plus English)

evidence.title: Transcribing multilingual radiologist-patient dialogue into mammography reports using AI: A step towards patient-centric radiology
evidence.outcome: Ambient transcription accuracy (WER, CER) for Hindi radiologist-patient conversations
evidence.effect: Lowest WER 0.577 and CER 0.379 at temperature 0 for Hindi transcription with Whisper large-v2, indicating poor non-English transcription accuracy.
evidence.quote: The lowest WER (0.577) and CER (0.379) were observed at temperature 0.

evidence.title: Screening/diagnosis of pediatric endocrine disorders through the artificial intelligence model in different language settings
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT response reliability and quality by language (Chinese vs English)
evidence.effect: Unreliable rate 7.5% for English vs 27.5% for Chinese questions; among reliable answers, English responses were more comprehensive and satisfactory.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT performed better when responding to questions in English, with an unreliable rate of 7.5% compared to 27.5% for Chinese questions, indicating a more consistent response pattern in English.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (each posed three times in Chinese and English)

evidence.title: The utility of ChatGPT as a generative medical translator
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: GPT-4 response quality (PEMAT-P total score) by language: English, Spanish, Mandarin
evidence.effect: Total PEMAT-P scores differed by language (Eta-Square 0.07, scores 73-77, P=0.03); understandability (P=0.17), actionability (P=0.44), and procedure-specific accuracy (P=0.22) did not differ.
evidence.quote: Total PEMAT-P scores differed between English, Mandarin, and Spanish GPT-4 generated responses depicting a moderate effect size of language, Eta-Square 0.07 with scores ranging from 73 to 77 (P-value = 0.03).
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 responses to patient questions from otolaryngology guidelines

evidence.title: Language-adaptive artificial intelligence: assessing CHATGPT'S answer to frequently asked questions on total hip arthroplasty questions
evidence.venue: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated satisfaction of ChatGPT answers to hip arthroplasty FAQs by language (English vs Urdu)
evidence.effect: English: 9/10 satisfactory with minimal clarification, 1/10 moderate. Urdu (Roman and Nastaliq): 1/10 satisfactory with moderate clarification, 9/10 unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification.
evidence.quote: In both Roman and Nastaliq script Urdu, 1 (10%) answer was satisfactory requiring moderate clarification, while 9 (90%) were unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification.

evidence.title: Transcending Language Barriers: Can ChatGPT Be the Key to Enhancing Multilingual Accessibility in Health Care?
evidence.venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT report simplification quality (correctness, harm, completeness, term explanation) by output language
evidence.effect: Spanish outperformed Hindi and Russian in categories 1 and 3 (P<.05); Hindi worse than English in all four categories (P<.05); all translations worse than English in term explanation (P<.001).
evidence.quote: The Spanish translation outperformed the Hindi and Russian version significantly in categories 1 and 3 (P < .05).

evidence.title: Assessing ChatGPT as a Medical Consultation Assistant for Chronic Hepatitis B: Cross-Language Study of English and Chinese
evidence.outcome: Language-stratified performance of ChatGPT responses to CHB questions (English vs Chinese)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 performed better in English, particularly in informativeness and consistency across repeated queries; ChatGPT-4.0 overcame the language impact on information accuracy.
evidence.quote: Notably, superior performance was evident in English, particularly in terms of informativeness and consistency across repeated queries.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (English and Chinese) about chronic hepatitis B

evidence.title: Automatic structuring of radiology reports with on-premise open-source large language models
evidence.outcome: LLM report structuring accuracy (MCC) in English versus German reports
evidence.effect: Average MCC 0.75 (94% HDI 0.70-0.80) for English versus 0.66 (0.62-0.70) for German; LLM-human MCC differences within ROPE for both languages.
evidence.quote: However, the understanding of semantics varied across languages and imaging findings.
evidence.sample_unit: chest radiograph reports (202 English MIMIC-CXR, 197 German)

evidence.title: The potential of Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 (GPT-4) to analyse medical notes in three different languages: a retrospective model-evaluation study
evidence.outcome: Physician agreement with GPT-4 responses on medical notes, stratified by note language
evidence.effect: Both physicians agreed with GPT-4 in 88% (86/98) of Spanish, 84% (82/98) of Italian, and 77% (454/588) of English responses; non-English performance was not worse.
evidence.quote: Both physicians agreed with GPT-4 more often for medical notes written in Spanish (86 [88%, 95% CI 79-93] of 98 responses) and Italian (82 [84%, 75-90] of 98 responses) than in English (454 [77%, 74-80] of 588 responses).
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 responses (14 questions on each of 56 medical notes)

evidence.title: Advancing health equity: evaluating AI translations of kidney donor information for Spanish speakers
evidence.outcome: Linguistic accuracy of AI Spanish translations rated by native-speaking nephrologists (1-5)
evidence.effect: Mean linguistic accuracy 4.89 ± 0.32 for GPT-3.5 and 5.00 ± 0.00 for GPT-4.0 (p = 0.08); excellent translations 89% vs 100% (p = 0.24).
evidence.quote: The mean linguistic accuracy scores were 4.89 ± 0.32 for GPT-3.5 and 5.00 ± 0.00 for GPT-4.0 (p = 0.08).

evidence.title: Evaluation of the accuracy and safety of machine translation of patient-specific discharge instructions: a comparative analysis
evidence.outcome: Translation accuracy of ED discharge instructions by target language (Spanish, Chinese, Russian)
evidence.effect: Sentence-level accuracy: GPT 97%, 95%, 89% and Google Translate 96%, 90%, 80% for Spanish, Chinese, Russian; instruction sets with at least one inaccuracy: GPT 16%, 24%, 56%; Google 24%, 56%, 66%.
evidence.quote: At the instruction set level, 16%, 24% and 56% of Spanish, Chinese and Russian GPT-translated instruction sets contained at least one inaccuracy.
evidence.sample_unit: sentences (50 deidentified ED discharge instruction sets)

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Ptosis-Related inquiries: A Cross-Lingual Study
evidence.outcome: LLM response clarity by language (Chinese vs English) rated by patients
evidence.effect: Qwen2.5 exhibited superior Chinese-language clarity compared to English (P = 0.023); GPT-4o excelled in English; other cross-language differences not reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Qwen2.5 exhibited superior Chinese-language clarity compared to English (P = 0.023).
evidence.sample_unit: questions (11 patient-centric, 50 doctor-centric) rated by 30 patients and 8 oculoplastic surgeons

evidence.title: Can machine translation match human expertise? Quantifying the performance of large language models in the translation of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs)
evidence.outcome: Machine translation quality (METEOR) variation across target languages
evidence.effect: Forward translation METEOR scores varied significantly by target language for all MT tools (p<0.001); scores differed among translators for all languages except Italian (p=0.59).
evidence.quote: In forward translations, the METEOR scores significantly varied depending on target languages for all MT tools (p < 0.001), with GPT-4 having the highest scores in most languages.
evidence.sample_unit: PROM scales translated (Breast-Q and Face-Q scales)
evidence.country: Multinational (Arabic, Vietnamese, Italian, Hungarian, Malay, Dutch target languages)

evidence.title: Evaluation of GPT-4o for multilingual translation of radiology reports across imaging modalities
evidence.outcome: Translation factual correctness and harmful errors stratified by target language
evidence.effect: Factual correctness averaged 79%, English 84% and French 83% versus Russian 69% (each p<0.05). Potentially harmful errors in 4% of translations, primarily Russian (9%).
evidence.quote: Factual correctness averaged 79 %, with English (84 %) and French (83 %) outperforming Russian (69 %) (each p < 0.05).

evidence.title: Bridging generative AI and healthcare practice: insights from the GenAI Health Hackathon at Hospital Clínic de Barcelona
evidence.outcome: Prototype performance on multilingual tasks
evidence.effect: Lower scores (F1<0.52, Jaccard Index <0.4) were seen in complex reasoning or multilingual tasks.
evidence.quote: Lower scores (F1<0.52, Jaccard Index <0.4) were seen in complex reasoning or multilingual tasks.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-guided translation of pediatric emergency department discharge instructions
evidence.outcome: Bilingual raters' accuracy, safety, understandability of translated discharge instructions, by language
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 more accurate than Google Translate in Arabic (4.1 vs 3.7, p=0.003) and Chinese (4.4 vs 4.2, p=0.010); no significant safety or understandability differences in either language.
evidence.quote: There were no significant differences in safety or understandability between ChatGPT-4 and Google Translate in either language.
evidence.sample_unit: discharge instruction documents translated (rated by 8 bilingual medical professionals)

evidence.title: Less time Coding, more time Caring: Performance evaluation of ChatGPT-5 for ICD-10 coding of radiology reports
evidence.outcome: ICD-10 coding concordance and coding time for non-English versus English radiology reports
evidence.effect: Non-English reports had significantly lower concordance (first character p=0.002; second/third characters p<0.001; last characters p=0.012) and longer coding times (p=0.002) than English reports.
evidence.quote: Coding non-English reports resulted in significantly lower concordance (first character: p = 0.002; second/third characters: p < 0.001; last characters: p = 0.012) and longer coding times than English reports (p = 0.002).
evidence.sample_unit: fictitious radiology reports (PARROT) plus 100 fictitious PET/CT reports

evidence.title: Large language models for frontline healthcare support in low-resource settings
evidence.outcome: LLM response quality when communicating in Kinyarwanda versus English
evidence.effect: Performance degraded slightly when LLMs communicated in Kinyarwanda, though LLMs remained superior to clinicians.
evidence.quote: Although performance degraded slightly when LLMs communicated in Kinyarwanda, the LLMs remained superior to clinicians and were over 500 times cheaper per response.

evidence.title: Do Large Language Models Perform Equally Across Languages? A Comparison of Responses to Frequently Asked Questions in Anesthesiology
evidence.venue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
evidence.outcome: LLM response quality in Turkish versus English for anesthesia patient questions
evidence.effect: English responses of ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 were rated superior to Turkish responses in overall, content, and communication quality (P<0.001 for most comparisons; P=0.001 for DeepSeek communication).
evidence.quote: English responses of ChatGPT 4.0 were superior to the Turkish responses in the terms of overall, content, and communication quality (P<0.001 each) and English responses of DeepSeek V3 were superior to the Turkish responses in the terms of overall (P<0.001), content (P<0.001) and communication (P=0.001) quality.
evidence.sample_unit: expert anesthesiologist raters evaluating responses to 10 FAQs

evidence.title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
evidence.outcome: Speech transcription error rates stratified by speaker language background (native vs non-native)
evidence.effect: Language-stratified analysis showed higher WER for non-native speakers across Whisper, WhisperX and WhisperX-GPT; disparity largest for Whisper (β = 11.0).
evidence.quote: Across all three ASR systems (Whisper, WhisperX, and WhisperX-GPT) non-native speakers consistently demonstrated higher WER, with the effect size varying by model.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence for tailoring complex clinical information to patients and families: A technical perspective
evidence.venue: The journal of spinal cord medicine
evidence.outcome: Cross-language consistency of readability classification for GPT-4o simplifications
evidence.effect: Readability classifications were not concordant across languages (3/10 cases, 30%); one simplified version was Plain English by FKGL but Fairly Difficult by FH.
evidence.quote: Readability classifications were not concordant across languages (3/10 cases, 30%); e.g. one simplified version was "Plain English" by FKGL but "Fairly Difficult" by FH, highlighting language-specific behavior.
evidence.country: Not reported (Spanish-language SCI clinical reports; likely Spain/US)

evidence.title: A hybrid large language model framework for structured data entry from code-switched persian clinical speech
evidence.outcome: Speech recognition error rates in Persian code-switched clinical speech
evidence.effect: Whisper WER 18.4% on standard Persian clinical speech, rising to 28.7% with heavy code-switching; Google Speech-to-Text WER 32.1%. Language-stratified performance was reported for code-switched segments.
evidence.quote: On the evaluation dataset, the Whisper model achieved a Word Error Rate (WER) of 18.4% on standard Persian clinical speech, increasing to 28.7% in segments exhibiting heavy code-switching.

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Translation Accuracy of Emergency Department Discharge Instructions: A Non-Inferiority Study
evidence.venue: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
evidence.outcome: Translation accuracy by language (fluency, adequacy, meaning, severity) versus professional interpreters
evidence.effect: Machine translation non-inferior for adequacy, meaning, severity in Spanish and Portuguese and all four domains in Chinese; fluency inferior in Spanish and Portuguese. Clinically significant error frequency did not differ by method.
evidence.quote: For fluency, Google Translate and ChatGPT-4o were inferior in Spanish and Portuguese but non-inferior in Chinese.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models for glaucoma counseling: A pilot study of ChatGPT and Google Gemini responses in Traditional Chinese
evidence.outcome: Appropriateness of LLM glaucoma answers in Traditional Chinese, rated by ophthalmologists on 5-point Likert
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 4.32 ± 0.65 vs Gemini 4.03 ± 0.66 (P = 0.004); both reasonably appropriate, lower on lifestyle questions; no language-stratified comparison with English.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT achieved a higher overall appropriateness score (4.32 ± 0.65) than Google Gemini (4.03 ± 0.66), with a statistically significant difference (P = 0.004).

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Turkish Emergency CT Impression Drafting: Quality, Critical Omissions, and Readability
evidence.venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
evidence.outcome: LLM impression quality and omissions for Turkish-language (non-English) reports
evidence.effect: Turkish CT impression quality varied by model and region; acceptable in selected settings but occasional critical omissions persisted.
evidence.quote: LLM-generated Turkish CT impressions can reach acceptable quality in selected settings, but occasional critical omissions persist.

evidence.title: Quality and safety of large language model generated communication in psychodermatology: a bilingual scenario-based evaluation
evidence.outcome: LLM response quality by language (English vs Turkish) across models
evidence.effect: LLaMA 3.1 showed significantly lower quality in Turkish (66.3%) than English (77.2%; P < 0.001); Gemini 2.5 Flash scored highest in both languages.
evidence.quote: LLaMA 3.1 showed significantly lower quality in Turkish (66.3%) compared with English (77.2%; P < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: standardized psychodermatology scenarios (each answered by 5 LLMs in English and Turkish, rated by 3 clinicians)

evidence.title: Assessment of Artificial Intelligence-based Translation Tools for Emergency Department Discharge Instructions
evidence.venue: The western journal of emergency medicine
evidence.outcome: AI translation quality of discharge instructions by target language and tool
evidence.effect: Overall scores similar (ChatGPT-4 3.79, Copilot 3.60, Google Translate 3.50); Albanian ChatGPT-4 3.75 vs Google Translate 3.19 (P<.001); no other significant language differences.
evidence.quote: Albanian translation was an exception, with ChatGPT-4 scoring significantly higher (3.75) than Google Translate (3.19) (P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: translated discharge instruction sets (4 topics x 3 languages x 3 tools)

evidence.title: Language-Specific Differences in Large Language Model Diagnostic Reasoning: A Translation-Controlled Clinical Vignette Study
evidence.outcome: LLM diagnostic reasoning score in English versus Polish across six models
evidence.effect: Qwen2.5, Llama3.3, Meditron3, and OpenBioLLM performed significantly better in English (largest gap for Qwen2.5); GPT-5 and Bielik showed no statistically detectable English-Polish difference in overall score.
evidence.quote: Qwen2.5, Llama3.3, Meditron3, and OpenBioLLM performed significantly better in English, with the largest gap observed for Qwen2.5.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical vignettes (real-patient cases, each in English and Polish, across six LLMs; 360 unique responses, 720 rater-level evaluations)

evidence.title: Impact of Query Language on the Structure and Guideline Alignment of AI-Generated Rehabilitation Programs in Chronic Kidney Disease
evidence.outcome: Guideline alignment and clinical depth of AI-generated CKD exercise programs by query language
evidence.effect: Ukrainian-language outputs were simpler, wellness-focused, with limited progression and monitoring; English-language outputs were more detailed, guideline-aligned, with structured progression and validated monitoring tools.
evidence.quote: English-language prompts produced more detailed and guideline-aligned outputs, whereas Ukrainian-language prompts generated simpler, wellness-oriented recommendations.
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated exercise programs (identical prompts in Ukrainian and English across three chatbots)

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT, Google Translate, and UD Talk for Chinese-to-Japanese Translation in Cardiology and Pulmonology Outpatient Consultations: Prospective Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Translation accuracy of AI tools for Chinese-to-Japanese outpatient consultations, by tool and specialty
evidence.effect: Google Translate and UD Talk median accuracy 2.0 (IQR 1.0-3.0) versus ChatGPT 5.0 (IQR 4.0-5.0), P<.001; ChatGPT consistent across cardiology and pulmonology.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT had significantly higher translation accuracy and satisfaction scores than Google Translate and UD Talk, with median scores of 5.0 (IQR 4.0-5.0) for both outcomes compared with 2.0 (IQR 1.0-3.0) for Google Translate and UD Talk (P<.001), and maintained a consistently high performance in both specialties.

evidence.title: Comparison of DeepSeek-V3.2 and ChatGPT-5.2 in the outpatient diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer: a multicenter evaluation of application value and multilingual adaptability
evidence.outcome: LLM performance by prompt language (Chinese vs English)
evidence.effect: Chinese: DeepSeek 4.40 ± 0.51 vs ChatGPT 4.25 ± 0.47 (P<0.001). English: ChatGPT 4.33 ± 0.38 vs DeepSeek 4.20 ± 0.49 (P<0.001).
evidence.quote: In the English environment, ChatGPT-5.2 outperformed DeepSeek-V3.2 (4.33 ± 0.38 vs. 4.20 ± 0.49, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Language-dependent performance variation in large language models for dental trauma management: a comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-5.2, Gemini 3.0, and Claude 4.5 Sonnet
evidence.outcome: LLM performance on dental trauma scenarios by query language (English vs Turkish)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT 9.14% higher in English (p<0.001); Gemini 5.69% English advantage (p=0.003); Claude language-independent (-0.02%, p=0.220).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT showed the strongest language effect with 9.14% higher performance in English (p < 0.001, r = 0.874).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (27 scenarios x 3 models x 2 languages)

evidence.title: Propagation of Interpreter Errors by Ambient AI Scribes: Study Using Simulated Clinical Encounters
evidence.outcome: Ambient AI scribe propagation of interpreter errors into notes in English and Spanish encounters
evidence.effect: Ambient AI scribes propagated interpreter errors into clinical notes, with patterns varying by speaker role and error type; no numbers in the abstract.
evidence.quote: In simulated English and Spanish clinical encounters, ambient AI scribes propagated interpreter errors into clinical notes, with patterns varying by speaker role and error type.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Translation of BI-RADS Breast Imaging Reports into Arabic: A Blinded Expert Evaluation of Diagnostic Communication Safety
evidence.outcome: Radiologist-rated quality and laterality accuracy of LLM Arabic translations of BI-RADS reports
evidence.effect: Overall mean scores: Gemini 3.73, DeepSeek 3.54, ChatGPT 3.03 (p<0.001); ChatGPT scored lower on all eight domains; no laterality errors among 15 translations.
evidence.quote: No laterality errors were identified among the 15 translations.

evidence.title: Diagnostic performance of large language models for discrepancy detection in non-English resident-authored abdominal CT and MRI reports: a Turkish-language evaluation.
evidence.outcome: LLM discrepancy detection sensitivity on non-English (Turkish) radiology reports by model
evidence.effect: Event-level sensitivity differed significantly among models (p < 0.001): Claude 93.4%, GPT-5.3 91.9%, Gemini 3.0 Pro 72.6%; Claude false-positive rate 0.6%.
evidence.quote: Claude 4.6 Sonnet achieved the highest overall sensitivity (93.4%), followed by GPT-5.3 (91.9%) and Gemini 3.0 Pro (72.6%).
evidence.sample_unit: abdominal CT and MRI report pairs

commentary.bottom_line: No study has tested whether language-stratified evaluation of ambient documentation detects or reduces errors, and the one study classed as testing the practice measured chatbot engagement rather than note quality. Hazard studies, including one of 54,160 outpatient encounters, suggest that ambient scribe performance can be lower in non-English encounters, which gives the recommendation a plausible rationale.

perspectives.view: The only study linked to the practice compared chatbot engagement in 1,282 limited English proficiency and English-primary patients and found 12.3 vs 12.2 text responses (P = .959). It stratified by language but did not assess ambient documentation, so indirectness is serious. With one study and no outcome on note accuracy, certainty is very low.

In a scripted study of 2,302 sessions, serious note errors rose from 7% to 10% to 15% as language resources became scarcer, while note generation alone showed no gradient. This suggests errors may enter at transcription, a stage that aggregate metrics can hide. No study shows that stratified monitoring catches these errors before they reach the chart.

A study of 54,160 outpatient encounters linked language to the share of unedited AI-generated words and found non-English encounters 21% to 25% less likely to meet the performance threshold. This suggests stratified analysis can run on routine deployment data. Results elsewhere vary, with Arabic notes scoring 4.53 vs 4.77 (P=.06) and simulated AI notes outscoring clinician notes in five languages.

The 54,160-encounter study included safety-net and non-English patients and found no difference between interpreter-mediated and bilingual provider encounters. In reenacted conversations, median mixed error rate was 9% for Mandarin-English, with outliers at 67%. In a UK survey of 141 GP scribe users, 31% named non-English encounters as an error setting. Language-specific reporting may reveal gaps a binary split hides.

The largest hazard study used an outcome, the share of unedited AI-generated words, that health systems may be able to compute from existing logs once encounter language is recorded. No study reports the cost or staff time of capturing language metadata or running stratified reviews, so the resource burden remains unmeasured.

When 400 machine translations of medical text were checked, 4% contained potentially harmful errors, and 9% of Russian translations did. Patients who speak less common languages may bear more of the error burden. Stratified evaluation could make that burden visible, but no study measures whether it improves patient safety or trust.

commentary.research_gap: No study has compared ambient documentation deployments with and without language-stratified monitoring to see whether stratification leads to detection and correction of errors in non-English notes. Studies are needed that capture encounter language, report error rates by specific language and interpreter use, track whether findings change vendor configuration, clinician review, or patient outcomes, and report the cost of doing so.
commentary.underserved_note: The one study classed as testing the practice included limited English proficiency patients but measured chatbot engagement, not documentation accuracy. Safety-net data appear only in a hazard study, and no test included Medicaid or low-literacy populations, so health systems serving these groups have no direct evidence that stratified evaluation works for them.
